text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand the issue with your right ring finger, can you describe exactly how the swelling and pain started? Did it begin suddenly after an injury or gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like a classic mechanism for a "jammed finger," which often involves ligament or tendon injury. Can you tell me if you are still able to fully bend and straighten the finger, or does it feel stuck or weak when you try to move it?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: This inability to actively flex the fingertip, combined with the injury mechanism, strongly suggests a mallet finger injury. Do you have any pain or swelling at the base of the finger near the palm, or is it strictly localized to the tip?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history and symptoms are classic for a mallet finger injury, where the tendon is either stretched or torn, preventing active flexion of the fingertip.
